value.answer: This sounds like it could be hand-foot-mouth disease - common in preschoolers, causing mouth sores, low fever, and spots on hands/feet. It's usually mild and clears in about a week. Offer cool fluids and soft foods since mouth sores can make eating/drinking hurt; watch for signs of not drinking enough.
value.triage: Call 811 if fever lasts more than a couple days, sores worsen, or your child is drinking poorly (fewer wet diapers, no tears). Go to the ER or call 911 if there's trouble breathing, stiff neck, unusual drowsiness, a rash that doesn't fade under pressure, signs of dehydration (no urine 8+ hrs, very dry mouth), or your child seems seriously unwell.
sources: CDC - Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease
